title: Repair audited operator workflow failures
summary: Repair nine confirmed operator workflow failures across Maintenance, Queue, Rename, Settings, Libraries, primary navigation, and release-builder defaults, with browser, native Tauri, Local API, packaging, and regression evidence.
reason: The functional audit found deterministic failures caused by missing injected WebView dependencies, inconsistent keyboard activation, byte/GiB metadata mismatch, incomplete patch-reset and inheritance semantics, imprecise guided links, and release defaults that did not select the verified test-inclusive package path.
behavior_before: Fresh-page Maintenance, Queue strategy, and Rename paths could throw ReferenceError exceptions; primary navigation keyboard activation was inconsistent; Settings rendered byte constraints as GiB values and reset controls could retain owned patch keys; Library empty overrides and guided links lost intent or targeted hidden/imprecise controls; release actions defaulted away from the verified test-inclusive package path.
behavior_after: Each WebView module uses explicit injected dependencies and safe fallbacks; all 15 primary pages activate exactly once with Enter or Space and suppress repeated Enter; byte constraints are converted only for byte-backed GiB fields; all ten builder resets prune only owned keys and malformed JSON blocks safely; Library inheritance preserves explicit-empty intent and guided links focus visible exact controls; release dry-run/build defaults include tests while the optional Tauri binary remains opt-in.
manual_validation: Canonical browser wrappers passed for Maintenance change ledger, Queue large table, Rename, Settings launch, and lifecycle navigation using isolated temporary state.
Targeted Python/WebView regression groups passed, including 43 release-default tests, 40 adjacent static/mutation tests, 29 Settings/Libraries static tests, and 23 frontend mutation-boundary tests.
Local API maintenance dry-run contract smoke and Settings patch-evidence smoke passed against temporary configuration roots.
Tauri CheckOnly/build passed, all 43 Rust tests passed, and the native WebView UI Automation probe passed all 30 Enter/Space navigation cases.

An actual release dry-run planned 18,108 copies and 10,046 exclusions with no writes; an actual test-inclusive package copied 18,109 files, passed tool integration and end-to-end smoke, and launched/closed successfully from isolated state.
Canonical package verification and ZIP creation remained blocked only by unrelated pre-existing lifecycle/generated-context/documentation drift; no bypass was used.
No source media, persistent operator state, FFmpeg policy, subtitle policy, audio policy, or publish behavior was exercised or changed; representative real-media validation is not required.
rollback_plan: Revert the listed WebView, Tauri probe, maintenance contracts/policy, tests, inventory, changelog, and generated-summary changes together. This restores the prior UI and release defaults; validation used only isolated temporary roots, so no media or persistent operator-state rollback is required.

Implementation followed TDD with captured RED failures for each defect and GREEN focused regressions. Two independent reviews identified and drove hardening for Rename degraded fallback, byte-unit guarding, and hidden guided-link targets; the final review reported no findings. Broad release and guardrail runs were attempted without weakening gates; their remaining failures are unrelated baseline drift outside this packet. No commit was created.
